title: Recycle handoff at the WCLI-11 / DEC-30 boundary
description: The recycle handoff written AFTER the recycler's fresh request (the WCLI-43/WCLI-45 shape), after WCLI-31 and WCLI-36 landed, WCLI-11's acceptance criteria were written and trimmed, and DEC-19 B, DEC-25, DEC-26 A and DEC-30 A were decided. It states the repository as it stands, points at WCLI-11 for the held implementation, and names the successor's first work: WCLI-11, then the promotion of dev.
implementationNotes:
RECYCLE HANDOFF, 2026-09-29, written and discharged in-session at the recycler's order (the WCLI-43/WCLI-45 shape), after four tracker changes landed and two design decisions were answered. The successor's briefing is in three parts: what finished, where things stand, and what comes next.

WHAT FINISHED THIS SESSION, each landed through its own PR with required checks green: WCLI-31 (opum-ai/ward-cli#86, squash b85a4d9) — the setup_in_progress message is exactly DEC-13's wording, pinned by a contract test, lock ordering untouched, reported at its boundary. WCLI-36 (opum-ai/ward-cli#87, squash 3daed97) — closed as superseded by DEC-18 A, citing the record, both criteria deliberately left unchecked with the reason on the task. WCLI-11's acceptance criteria, twice: written first (#88, squash c66fc53) and then trimmed after DEC-25 (#89, squash 5926098). Also earlier in the session: WCLI-35 landed (#82, 0595a92) and was promoted (#83), and two prior handoffs landed (#84, #85).

THE DECISIONS, each read first-hand from opum-ai/opum-agent origin/main dd17e45 (opum-ai/opum-agent#1364) except DEC-30, which was relayed as accepted and lands on that ref shortly: DEC-19 B — strict bump of vaultStateFormatVersion to 2; its recovery-story sentence is WITHDRAWN (opum-doc's gloss, not the operator's words). DEC-25 — NEITHER option: NO RECOVERY. Format-1 vaults are simply refused; there is no `ward migrate` and no read-out command; secrets in any existing v1 vault are lost to ward. DEC-26 A — keep the single vault_format_unsupported code, reword the message true at all three sites (sealed envelope, profile snapshot, state document), and DROP the hint. DEC-30 A — the string is exactly the one ward-cli proposed: "This vault was written by a different version of Ward, and this build cannot read it. Ward did not change it." Read each from its own record before building, not from a relay.

WHERE THINGS STAND, VERIFIED AT THIS WRITE. origin/dev is 5926098 (WCLI-11's trimmed ACs); origin/main is 0595a92, so dev is several commits ahead and a promotion is the successor's (the orchestrator's kickoff names it: "the promotion of your dev +6"). Working tree clean; local branches dev and main only; no open pull requests. quest task list --status "In Progress" on dev: WCLI-11 only, which is correct — its implementation is unstarted and remains held.

WHAT THE SUCCESSOR DOES FIRST. WCLI-11's implementation, against the four decisions above and the six criteria now on the task (positions 1-2 already checked, 3-6 the work). Nothing beyond those criteria exists in the tree. A 140-line parked patch at /tmp/wcli11-partial-implementation.patch carries the format-2 record shape, its validators, the serializer and the version bump — no recovery code, so DEC-25 does not obsolete it — but it is scratch on this machine's /tmp: verify it applies (`git apply --check`) before using it, and re-derive anything you cannot see. Then the promotion of dev to main by the documented fast-forward with its post-push assertions. WCLI-36 and WCLI-31 are done; do not reopen either.

SKILLS for the successor: opum-sdlc, opum-handoff, quest, lore.

RAILS: every probe this session ran against temporary stores and synthetic keys; nothing touched the developer's ~/.ward or a real keychain item; nothing was published. The cursor was written by the flush at this order (write mode) and is left in place; note the flush wrote no tracker note this time because two tasks were In Progress at the moment it ran — WCLI-11 and this handoff — which is its documented behaviour, not a failure. The cursor is the artifact the recycle gate needs.

DISCOVERY AT THE BOUNDARY, recorded so it is not lost: the working tree holds an UNTRACKED .quest/tasks/WCLI-46.json, created 2026-09-29T10:01:20.935Z — one minute before this handoff's task was created — by the remote-mgmt fleet session ('Test runs leak ward-packaged-* build dirs into TMPDIR (~1.1 GiB/hour on minim4)', To Do, no notes). It is not this session's record and it is left exactly as found: not staged, not committed, not edited, because its creator may still be writing it. That leaves it git-invisible, which is the one state .quest/ records are not supposed to be in — flagging it for the successor (land it if its owner does not) and for opum-agent. This is also why the handoff task allocated as WCLI-47: the allocator saw 46 in the working tree.
